native_mechanisms: A glint leaves the source jewel and crawls down each cord at a pace set by that cord's own length, so arrival time equals accumulated cord length (short cords flash at once, long cords keep the glint waiting).
Each jewel's square is chalked once at its first flare; any later flare arriving along a longer, slacker cord is thrown away unmarked.
A square that no flare ever reaches is left blank and crossed out (unreachable = no distance).
core_technique: Delta-stepping: distance/delta bucket (drawer) queue with per-vertex CSR split into light (<delta, drained within the current bucket until fixpoint) and heavy (deferred to bucket end) edges, no priority queue and no settled test — with a plain O(n^2) array-scan Dijkstra used only for small (n<=256) or dense (m >= 0.1n^2) graphs and as an allocation-failure fallback.
